riskDescription.context: Support has been extended at no additional cost until September 2026 without formal contractual clarity, and scope and delivery expectations are evolving without a formally approved SOW or CR.
riskDescription.condition: Remaining effort may continue without clear commercial coverage, creating revenue leakage and margin erosion.
riskDescription.consequence: The organization could incur unrecoverable costs, and the client may contest additional charges when formal commercials are eventually defined.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Establish formal change control process requiring customer approval and signed CR before executing any scope beyond September 2026 SOW.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Upon client contestation of charges, escalate to executive leadership with documented effort logs and activate legal review within 48 hours.
risks.reasoning: Open EMS risk R832 (Major/Very Likely/High Impact, raised 2026-07-15) corroborated by ALT Watchlist noting lack of defined end dates, scope boundaries, and commercials in original SOW and subsequent CR. OBS6482 (Open, aging 30 days) recommends finalizing CR strategy and documenting commercial approach. No mitigation has been implemented.

riskDescription.context: Scope and delivery expectations are evolving without a formally approved SOW or CR, and challenges exist in the clarity of the scope and features to be implemented in the Verify application.
riskDescription.condition: Additional scope may be requested or assumed without formal change control, leading to uncontrolled scope expansion.
riskDescription.consequence: Delivery timelines could extend indefinitely, team capacity may be consumed by unplanned work, and client expectations may diverge from what can be delivered within available resources.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Implement formal scope evaluation and approval procedure, documenting all requested changes and halting work until signed CR is received.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: If scope expands beyond capacity, escalate to customer leadership to rebaseline delivery plan and defer non-critical functionality to Phase 2.
risks.reasoning: Open EMS risks R831 and R832 (both Major/Very Likely/High Impact, raised 2026-07-15) describe evolving scope without formal approval. ALT Watchlist confirms challenges in scope clarity and lack of defined scope boundaries. OBS6482 (Open, aging 30 days) calls for direct customer leadership engagement to establish clarity on onboarding plans and future application scope. Mitigation identified but not yet arrived.

riskDescription.context: IBM Verify product implementation has encountered feature gaps and dependency-related delays due to ongoing alignment between IBM and Red Hat on scope and rollout timelines.
riskDescription.condition: Critical IAM and IGA capabilities may remain incomplete or unstable, requiring workarounds or extended development cycles.
riskDescription.consequence: Application onboarding could be delayed, business benefits realization postponed, and client confidence in the platform weakened.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Conduct weekly IBM Verify product roadmap reviews with vendor, tracking feature delivery commitments and escalating delays through formal support channels.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Once feature delay exceeds four weeks, activate alternative workaround solution and escalate to Red Hat executive sponsor for vendor intervention.
risks.reasoning: Open EMS risks R831 and R833 (both Major/Very Likely/High Impact, raised 2026-07-15) cite IBM Verify product limitations and dependency-related delays. ALT Watchlist confirms Verify implementation encountered feature gaps and dependency-related delays. No mitigation plan has been finalized.

riskDescription.context: The project relies on IBM for product fixes and feature enablement, and ongoing alignment between IBM and Red Hat on scope and rollout timelines is required.
riskDescription.condition: IBM may not deliver required fixes or features within the project's timeline, or alignment discussions may extend without resolution.
riskDescription.consequence: Delivery could stall, critical functionality may remain unavailable, and the project may miss contractual or business-driven go-live commitments.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Monitor IBM support ticket resolution timelines weekly, escalating priority-1 issues to IBM account manager and building two-week buffer into delivery schedule.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Should IBM fix delay exceed committed SLA by five business days, engage backup vendor for workaround and notify Red Hat leadership.
risks.reasoning: Open EMS risks R832 and R833 (both Major/Very Likely/High Impact, raised 2026-07-15) note reliance on IBM for product fixes and ongoing alignment requirements. ALT Watchlist confirms dependency-related delays due to ongoing alignment between IBM and Red Hat. External dependency with no committed resolution timeline.

riskDescription.context: Following the Red Hat–IBM organizational transition effective 1 October 2026, limited stakeholder availability for key decisions is creating uncertainty around project continuity, resource utilization, delivery timelines, and future funding.
riskDescription.condition: Key decisions may be delayed or deferred due to unclear ownership or competing priorities during the organizational merger.
riskDescription.consequence: Project direction could become ambiguous, critical approvals may be held up, and team productivity may decline due to lack of clear guidance.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Establish weekly governance touchpoint with Red Hat and IBM leadership, documenting decision ownership and maintaining escalation path to executive sponsors.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: When decision approval exceeds five business days, escalate to joint Red Hat-IBM steering committee and communicate impact to delivery timeline.
risks.reasoning: Open EMS risks R832 and R833 (both Major/Very Likely/High Impact, raised 2026-07-15) cite limited stakeholder availability for key decisions following the Red Hat–IBM organizational transition. ALT Watchlist confirms Red Hat IT and Security operations are merging with IBM starting 1 October 2026. OBS6482 (Open, aging 30 days) recommends continuing direct engagement with customer leadership. Organizational change is active and ongoing.

riskDescription.context: The Red Hat–IBM organizational transition is creating uncertainty around resource utilization and project continuity, though the team will continue with the same team strength.
riskDescription.condition: Client-side resource availability or engagement levels may decline during the transition, or internal team members may face competing priorities or reassignment.
riskDescription.consequence: Sprint velocity could drop, knowledge transfer may be incomplete, and the project may lose critical domain expertise or client-side support.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Conduct monthly resource continuity reviews with Red Hat, documenting key roles and maintaining cross-training plan for critical knowledge areas.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: If client-side engagement drops below 50 percent, engage backup SME from Ascendion bench and communicate capacity impact to customer leadership.
risks.reasoning: Open EMS risks R832 and R833 (both Major/Very Likely/High Impact, raised 2026-07-15) note uncertainty around resource utilization. ALT Watchlist confirms team will continue with same team strength, but organizational merger may affect client-side engagement. Single-source indication of potential impact; no evidence of current disruption.

riskDescription.context: The Producer Portal application is fully deployed to Production and technically ready for producer onboarding. Premera is planning to send registration emails to 2,500+ producers on October 22 using a big-bang rollout approach, with status awaited.
riskDescription.condition: If an issue is encountered during the mass producer onboarding, the rollout may need to be rolled back and remediated.
riskDescription.consequence: Go-live timeline could be delayed, client trust in release quality may be weakened, and remediation effort could consume planned capacity for other deliverables.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Validate Producer Portal with phased pilot group of 100 users before full rollout, monitoring error rates and performance against defined thresholds.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: If critical issue affects more than 5 percent of users, activate rollback procedure within two hours and engage war room support.
risks.reasoning: ALT Watchlist explicitly identifies this as a risk: 'If an issue is encountered during the mass producer onboarding, the rollout may need to be rolled back and remediated.' Big-bang approach for 2,500+ users carries inherent risk. End-to-end testing with 11 users completed successfully as of 22 October, but production-scale validation is pending. Single-source indication; no evidence of current issues.

riskDescription.context: Lack of application onboarding has contributed to prolonged delivery timelines and delayed realization of business benefits. Three additional applications have been identified for onboarding, indicating continued customer demand.
riskDescription.condition: If application onboarding does not accelerate or if additional applications are added without corresponding capacity or timeline adjustments, the backlog may grow.
riskDescription.consequence: Customer satisfaction could decline due to unmet expectations, and the business case for the IGA/IAM platform may be questioned if adoption remains low.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Define application onboarding roadmap with Red Hat, prioritizing three identified applications and establishing monthly onboarding velocity targets with capacity allocation.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: If onboarding backlog exceeds six applications, engage customer leadership to reprioritize scope and communicate revised timeline with phased delivery approach.
risks.reasoning: Open EMS risk R831 (Major/Very Likely/High Impact, raised 2026-07-15) cites lack of application onboarding contributing to prolonged delivery timelines. EMS OBS6481 (Open, aging 30 days) notes three additional applications identified for onboarding. OBS6482 recommends using current onboarding momentum to identify additional IAM and IGA opportunities. Demand exists, but execution pace is uncertain.

riskDescription.context: OBS6482 recommends continuing weekly status reporting to ensure leadership has visibility into onboarding progress, contract status, and customer dependencies. No evidence of current reporting cadence or leadership engagement is provided.
riskDescription.condition: If weekly status reporting is not established or maintained, leadership may lack timely visibility into critical project risks and dependencies.
riskDescription.consequence: Escalation triggers may be missed, corrective actions may be delayed, and executive support may not be mobilized when needed.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Implement weekly executive status report covering onboarding progress, contract status, and dependencies, distributed to Red Hat and Ascendion leadership by Friday.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: If critical risk emerges between weekly reports, trigger ad-hoc executive briefing within 24 hours and update status dashboard immediately.
risks.reasoning: EMS OBS6482 (Open, aging 30 days) explicitly recommends continuing weekly status reporting to ensure leadership visibility. Recommendation implies current reporting may be insufficient or inconsistent. Single-source indication; no evidence of current reporting gaps, but proactive recommendation suggests risk.
